Selected work (03)

Three systems, built to hold up.

01 AI agent runtime · 2026

Rewind

Kill the worker halfway through a refund. The customer still gets paid exactly once.

Every step of the agent is written to a Postgres event log before the next one starts, so another worker can pick up where the first one fell over. A debugger replays and forks any run without touching the real world.

  • TypeScript
  • Node.js
  • PostgreSQL
  • Fastify
  • React
Read the code ↗

rewind — demo:crash

  1. $ npm run demo:crash
  2. refund order A-100
  3. kill -9 worker-1 after the refund, before it was recorded
  4. worker-2 takes over the run
  5. refunds: 1   emails: 1  ✓ exactly once

Chaos test · 1,000 refund runs · 8 workers · a worker killed every 100 ms

02 Retrieval & evaluation · 2026

Dutch government RAG

Answers Dutch questions from Rijksoverheid.nl, cites its sources, and says so when it doesn’t know.

I compared four ways of finding text on a versioned set of 112 questions, checked the answers with an LLM judge, and then checked the judge by hand. It runs in Docker on Google Cloud Run with spending limits, and CI guards the scores on every push.

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • sentence-transformers
  • scikit-learn
  • Cloud Run
Read the code ↗

Judge checked by hand: 10 of 11 verdicts held up. A classifier for “can I answer this?” scored F1 0.76 against 0.73 for a simple threshold. Too close to ship, so I didn’t.

03 B2B automation · private system

Multiple Leadflow Generator

One outreach workflow for four audiences, with source checks and human review before a Gmail draft is created.

The dashboard brings the research and the proposed message into one place. The operator checks the evidence and the copy before anything is drafted. Nothing is sent automatically.

  • Research
  • Source checks
  • Human review
  • Gmail

Private system I built and use for my own studio, Magnifize. No public code.

  1. ResearchFind organisations for the selected audience.
